scheme_name: PMMSY: Large Fish Feed Mill of Production Capacity of 20 Ton /Day Scheme - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India aimed at enhancing fish production and promoting sustainable aquaculture. 

The scheme was officially launched on September 10, 2020. 

It is part of the broader initiative to increase the income of fishers and fish farmers. 

The PMMSY aims to achieve a fish production target of 22 million metric tons by 2024-2025. 

The scheme also focuses on creating employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

One of the significant components of PMMSY is the establishment of large fish feed mills. 

The specific project under consideration is the Large Fish Feed Mill of Production Capacity of 20 Ton/Day in Haryana. 

This project is designed to support the aquaculture sector by ensuring the availability of quality fish feed. 

Quality fish feed is crucial for enhancing the growth and productivity of fish. 

The establishment of this feed mill is expected to significantly reduce the dependency on imported fish feed. 

The mill will produce high-quality fish feed that meets the nutritional requirements of various fish species. 

The estimated investment for setting up a large fish feed mill in Haryana is approximately INR 1 crore. 

The Government of India provides a subsidy of up to 40% for setting up such feed mills. 

This means that a maximum subsidy of INR 40 lakh can be availed by the beneficiaries. 

The primary objective of this initiative is to enhance fish production in the state of Haryana. 

The scheme aims to increase the income of fish farmers by providing them with access to affordable and quality fish feed. 

The target beneficiaries of this scheme include fish farmers, entrepreneurs, and cooperatives involved in aquaculture. 

Eligibility criteria for availing benefits under this scheme include being a registered fish farmer or entrepreneur. 

There are no specific age limits mentioned for eligibility. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a commitment to aquaculture practices. 

The application process for the Large Fish Feed Mill involves several steps. 

Interested applicants must first submit a project proposal to the Department of Fisheries in Haryana. 

The proposal should include details about the production capacity, technology to be used, and financial projections. 

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, and proof of land ownership or lease. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it will be evaluated by a committee formed by the Department of Fisheries. 

If approved, the applicant will receive a letter of sanction along with the subsidy amount. 

The timeline for the entire application process can vary but typically takes around 2 to 3 months. 

Disbursement of the subsidy amount is usually done in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The first installment is released upon the approval of the project. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the completion of specific milestones. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Fisheries, Government of Haryana. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries can be found on the official Haryana government website. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of sustainable practices in aquaculture. 

This includes promoting the use of environmentally friendly feed ingredients. 

The PMMSY aims to create a robust supply chain for fish feed production. 

This will help in stabilizing fish prices and ensuring food security. 

The scheme is expected to generate significant employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

It is projected that the establishment of the feed mill will create around 50 direct jobs. 

Additionally, it will support numerous indirect jobs in the supply chain. 

The PMMSY also aims to promote research and development in fish feed technology. 

This includes exploring alternative feed ingredients to reduce costs. 

The scheme is aligned with the National Fisheries Policy of 2020. 

The policy aims to promote sustainable and responsible fishing practices. 

The PMMSY is funded through a combination of central and state government contributions. 

The central government contributes 60% of the total project cost. 

The state government contributes 20% while the remaining 20% is borne by the beneficiaries. 

The scheme also focuses on capacity building and skill development for fish farmers. 

Training programs are organized to educate farmers about best practices in aquaculture. 

The PMMSY also encourages the formation of self-help groups among fish farmers. 

These groups can help in collective bargaining and accessing resources more efficiently. 

The scheme is expected to have a multiplier effect on the rural economy. 

By increasing fish production, it will enhance the livelihoods of fishing communities. 

The PMMSY also aims to improve the nutritional standards of the population. 

Fish is a rich source of protein and essential nutrients. 

The establishment of the Large Fish Feed Mill is a critical step towards achieving these objectives. 

It will ensure that fish farmers have access to quality feed at affordable prices. 

The scheme is part of the Government of India’s broader vision to make India a global leader in fisheries. 

The PMMSY is expected to contribute significantly to the overall economic growth of the fisheries sector. 

The initiative is also in line with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations. 

The PMMSY aims to promote responsible and sustainable fishing practices. 

The establishment of the feed mill will play a vital role in achieving these goals. 

The scheme is a testament to the Government of India's commitment to the welfare of fishers and fish farmers. 

It reflects a comprehensive approach to enhancing the fisheries sector in India. 

The Large Fish Feed Mill of Production Capacity of 20 Ton/Day in Haryana is a significant project under this scheme. 

It is expected to bring about transformative changes in the aquaculture landscape of the state. 

The successful implementation of this project will serve as a model for similar initiatives across the country. 

The PMMSY is a forward-looking scheme that addresses the challenges faced by the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a sustainable and profitable environment for fish farming in India.
